knowledge_point.title: Identifying the Shift Applied to an Exponential Growth Curve

question.:question/problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186087822/plots/shift-asymptote-1.2/d8f157a099c9b201c2b82fd430bdb5288a3bcbe3fdc07a81039cd837b7e27e43.png)

The graph above shows the curve $y={(\frac{53}{6})}^{x}+c.$ Determine the value of $c$ and find the equation of the curve.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The horizontal asymptote of $y={(\frac{53}{6})}^{x}$ is $y=0.$ The vertical translation $y={(\frac{53}{6})}^{x}+c$ shifts the asymptote to $y=c.$

In the graph above, the horizontal asymptote is $y=\frac{3}{5}.$ Therefore, $c=\frac{3}{5}.$
